facts: WAWebBuildConstants exports VERSION_PRIMARY, VERSION_SECONDARY, VERSION_TERTIARY, VERSION_BASE and VERSION_STR as scalar properties, plus Windows-specific helpers and other origin/build properties. These version fields are not getter functions.

The same 1500-byte WAWebBuildConstants definition occurs in the original frontend, backend and service-worker bundles. Its shared module SHA256 is 6fa9be24d333f531b09ed962fa9fe1d7e6b6ce47792b4e77397955bcacfb80b6.

For either gate 26258 or 26259, VERSION_BASE uses 2.3000.<SiteData.client_revision>; otherwise it is 3.0.0. Suffix is empty, .i or .d according to those gates; Windows may append its separate build. Therefore VERSION_STR alone is not a unique revision authority.
StaticSiteData maps request parameter names; it does not provide the runtime numeric client revision. SiteData is supplied through dynamic bootstrap modules.
The reviewed service-worker entry declares public client_revision 1050806504 and imports the exact retained static dependency. The entry body includes dynamic metadata and was discarded.
runtimeIdentity.revisionScope: Only this service-worker entry and its directly referenced asset are bound by this observation. It does not establish the numeric revision of previously fetched frontend/backend assets or any installed/live account.

recommendation.classification: Design inference, not implemented or runtime-tested
recommendation.text: A future fixed adapter should require an explicitly supported numeric SiteData.client_revision and verified module/export contract, with unknown or changed identities failing closed. A generic VERSION_STR such as 3.0.0.d or the service-worker revision alone must not authorize an unrelated frontend bundle.

facts: AppBootstrap initializes /sw.js with scope /. Registration checks serviceWorker support and absence of the current controller, then uses updateViaCache all.
An AB-configured Safari standalone-PWA path unregisters registrations; PWA detection is display-mode standalone. This is conditional and is not a universal WKWebView exclusion.
ServiceWorkerSupport alive checks only navigator.serviceWorker.controller. No controller does not prove no registration, worker lifetime, or future claim.
SW install handlers are followed by skipWaiting; activate claims clients. updateSw updates registration/controller state but does not drain all persistent writers.

backgroundWrites.classification: Conditional source paths, not observed execution in ProfileDesk WKWebView

conditions: canSupportOfflineNotifications rejects recognized Safari versions below 16 and parsing errors.

Offline resume requires persisted worker treatment, Notification.permission granted, a non-null registration.pushManager.getSubscription() result, no window clients, no active communications, and a non-aborted resume signal.

Frontend subscription eligibility additionally requires enabled offline notifications, canEnableOfflineNotifications and screen lock disabled. Actual subscription also requires available browser registration/pushManager APIs and provider settings/configuration.
Calls use a distinct payload/handler branch; those are not evidence that the normal offline-resume branch always runs.
writes: The eligibility read initializes WorkerStorage and can clear persisted offline-resume treatment when permission/subscription is missing.
initializeDb loads schema versions and initializes Signal, Model, Worker, Offd and FTS storage.
handlePushNotification checks stored versions/settings, increments persistent offlinePushCount, initializes encryption salt and may start the backend worker in passive mode.
push.reachability: This static review does not establish PushManager/Notification support, granted permissions, a subscription, treatment state, or push delivery for the app WKWebView. Do not label this path active on iPhone from source presence.

conditions: canSupportPeriodicBackgroundSync returns false for recognized Safari, Firefox and Chrome below 80.
The handler additionally requires justknob 2337 false, the background-sync tag, no in-progress work or communications, and no window clients.
writes: When eligible, it initializes the same application stores and starts notification/backend processing.
periodic.reachability: The reviewed browser gate excludes recognized Safari. No periodicSync delivery was observed or proved on WKWebView.

facts: Sw creates a CacheHelper for wa-stickers as part of handler initialization; the constructor calls caches.open. Thus cache creation/opening is possible independently of a user sticker request.

SwObjectStores opens the sw IndexedDB database at version 2 with prefs, pp and stickers. Its helpers expose readwrite transactions, put/delete/clear; reads also use readwrite transactions. Upgrade code recreates stores. These helpers must not be invoked as harmless read-only export utilities.
CacheHelper exposes cache writes/deletes/reset/cleanup. fetchAndPut starts a cache put without awaiting it. Cache mutation is therefore not covered by a communications-only completion promise.

Notification click handling has fixed action routing. Its no-window path can initialize ModelStorage and update engagement before opening a window. A click is a user interaction, not proof of an autonomous idle write.

lifecycleBarrier.observed: The action cancels the current offline-resume AbortController and awaits interruptOfflineResume. When an offline process stage exists, the latter interrupts the resume manager and may await WAComms.stopComms.
insufficient: STOP_COMMS does not call blockOfflineResume; it does not establish an irreversible block against future push work.
No all-database close, all-cache flush, complete worker shutdown or registration suspension contract is shown in these definitions.
The database-version-change listener calls blockOfflineResume, but deliberately forcing a schema/version change is not an established safe backup barrier and is not recommended.
A closed/destroyed view, no controller, or communications stopped must not be equated with a globally consistent origin snapshot.
lifecycleBarrier.coldProcessProposal: A fresh native process with an inert importer could avoid starting official document code. Whether prior WebProcesses/service workers and persistent writes have stopped, and whether all mutable stores are consistent, requires platform evidence and an explicit capture design. This review provides no such guarantee.

facts: SwBase selects a fixed matching handler for each action; it is not a generic arbitrary function evaluator.
Page SWBus responses check the current service-worker controller source; envelopes carry action, message and VERSION_STR. This version field inherits the non-uniqueness limitation above.
swMessageRouting.privacyReview: Detailed fixed-handler and per-document callback/lock-ownership review is owned by native_messaging_ui under build/native-chat-public-review/fresh-view-lock-ownership. This report does not authorize native content projection.

remainingUnknowns: Exact live frontend revision and compatibility contract for any future adapter.
Actual WKWebView background capabilities and worker/process persistence under the proposed native lifecycle.
A consistent capture/import boundary across mutable protocol stores, persisted action queues, CacheStorage and all live writers.
An independent authenticated session-and-information restore proof.
claimsExcluded: No proof that complete migration is universally impossible.
No claim that every SW branch is active on iOS.
No full backup implementation, native adapter activation, account operation or deployment occurred.
